content_voiceover: This slide covers KMT2A rearranged ALL, one of the highest risk genetic subtypes, especially in infants. The top panel shows a modern treatment backbone that adds blinatumomab early, right after induction, before moving into Protocol IB, then MARMA and OCTADAD consolidation blocks, and finally maintenance. Medium risk patients who still have measurable residual disease of five times ten to the minus four or higher before OCTADAD, and all high risk patients, are triaged to stem cell transplant. The bottom panels show why this matters. Compared with the older Interfant zero six regimen, the current blinatumomab containing study nearly doubles two year disease free survival, eighty one point six percent versus forty nine point four percent, and substantially improves two year overall survival, ninety three point three percent versus sixty five point eight percent. For boards, remember that incorporating blinatumomab into infant KMT2A rearranged ALL therapy is a major recent practice change with strong survival benefit, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in twenty twenty three.
keypoints: Blinatumomab added early in KMT2A rearranged ALL therapy
Transplant reserved for high risk and MRD positive medium risk patients
Two year disease free survival roughly doubled versus Interfant zero six
Two year overall survival improved from about sixty six to ninety three percent
keypoint_voiceover: Key points to remember. Blinatumomab is now added early in the treatment course for KMT2A rearranged ALL. Transplant is reserved for high risk patients and for medium risk patients who remain MRD positive before OCTADAD. This approach roughly doubled two year disease free survival compared with Interfant zero six, and pushed two year overall survival up to about ninety three percent.
